overview.title: Overview
overview.text: Trimbakeshwar Temple, located in the town of Trimbak near Nashik, is an ancient and sacred Jyotirlinga shrine. It is unique because the lingam here embodies the three primary deities of Hinduism: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. The temple is also the source of the holy Godavari River.

mythology.title: Mythological Origin
mythology.text: The origin of the temple is linked to the sage Gautama Rishi. He performed a severe penance to bring the River Ganga here to absolve himself of the sin of cow-slaughter. The river came to be known as Godavari. To purify the sage, Lord Shiva decided to reside here in the form of the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga.

architecture.title: Architectural Highlights
points: The temple is built of black stone in the Nagara style of architecture.
It is situated at the foothills of Brahmagiri mountain, from where the Godavari originates.
The main lingam is in a depression on the floor, and a mirror placed on the wall allows devotees to see the three-faced deity inside.
The temple structure is adorned with exquisite sculptures and carvings.
The current temple was built by Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao in the 18th century.

significance.title: Spiritual Significance
points: It is the only Jyotirlinga where the lingam represents the Trimurti: Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh.
It is the source of the Godavari River, known as the 'Ganga of the South'.
The nearby Kushavarta Kund is the symbolic origin of the river and a sacred bathing spot.
Nashik-Trimbak is one of the four holy sites where the Kumbh Mela is held every 12 years.

events.event: Linked to the epic Ramayana, as Nashik is believed to be the 'Panchavati' forest.
The existing temple was constructed by the Maratha ruler, Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao.

items.text: Performing specific rituals like Kalsarp Puja here is believed to remove astrological afflictions.
The lingam is adorned with a jeweled crown, which is displayed every Monday.
A holy dip in the Kushavarta Kund is considered essential for a complete pilgrimage.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Trimbakeshwar is a confluence of divine energies, representing the unity of the cosmos. A pilgrimage here is a journey to the sacred source of the Godavari and an opportunity to witness the divine trinity in a singular, powerful form.

aboutPostCards.title: Major Festivals
items: Kumbh Mela – The grandest festival held once every 12 years.
Maha Shivratri – Celebrated with great fervor and special pujas.
Rath Yatra – A chariot festival held during Tripuri Purnima.

aboutPostCards.title: Nearby Attractions
items: Brahmagiri Hill – The source of the Godavari, a popular trekking spot.
Kushavarta Kund – The sacred pond for holy dips.
Panchavati – The area in Nashik city associated with the Ramayana.
Sula Vineyards – A famous winery near Nashik for a different kind of experience.

methods.title: By Road
methods.description: Trimbak is about 30 km from Nashik city. Nashik is well-connected by road to Mumbai, Pune, and other major cities.

methods.title: Nearest Railway
methods.description: Nashik Road Railway Station (NK) is the nearest major railhead.

methods.title: Nearest Airport
methods.description: Nashik Airport (ISK) has limited connectivity. Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai (BOM) is about 180 km away.
